title: Forwarding Refs
description: Learn how to pass refs through components to their children.

data.text: **Ref forwarding** lets a component receive a ref from its parent and pass it down to a child DOM element. This is essential for building reusable component libraries where the parent needs direct access to a nested element.
By default, refs are not passed through components like props. If a parent gives a ref to a functional component, it receives null unless the component explicitly forwards it.

data.title: Without forwardRef
data.content: Ref does not reach the child DOM element

data.text: Wrap the component with `forwardRef`. The ref becomes the second argument. Assign it to the child DOM element.

data.title: forwardRef

data.text: For more control, use `useImperativeHandle` with forwardRef. It lets you expose only specific methods to the parent, hiding the rest of the child implementation.

data.title: useImperativeHandle
data.content: Exposing a limited API to the parent

data.title: When to Forward Refs
items: Building reusable input components that need focus management.
Creating button components that need to trigger animations.
Wrapping third-party components that accept refs.
Exposing specific methods from a child to a parent.

data.title: Avoid Overusing forwardRef
data.text: Only forward refs when the parent genuinely needs DOM access. If the child can handle the behavior internally, keep the ref private.

terms.definition: A React utility that passes a ref through a component to a child.
A hook that customizes the instance value exposed to parent refs.

data.caption: How forwardRef passes a parent ref through to a child DOM node.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Focusable Button
data.description: Create a custom button that forwards its ref and exposes focus.
steps: Create a CustomButton component using forwardRef.
Forward the ref to the underlying <button>.
Create a parent component that holds a ref to the custom button.
Add a 'Focus Button' button that calls ref.current.focus().
data.expectedOutcome: A custom button that can be focused programmatically through a forwarded ref.

items.question: Do I need forwardRef for class components?
items.answer: No. Class components automatically receive refs as instance properties. forwardRef is only needed for function components.

items.question: Can I pass a ref to any component?
items.answer: To DOM elements and class components, yes. To function components, only if they are wrapped in forwardRef.

items.question: Why use useImperativeHandle instead of forwarding the raw ref?
items.answer: It protects the child's internals by exposing only the methods you choose. The parent cannot access private state or methods.

items.question: Is forwardRef used in production libraries?
items.answer: Yes. Material UI, Chakra UI, React Bootstrap, and most component libraries use forwardRef to let consumers access underlying DOM nodes.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: forwardRef passes parent refs through function components.
The ref is the second argument to the forwarded component.
useImperativeHandle exposes a limited API to the parent.
Use forwarding when building reusable component libraries.
data.takeaway: Forwarding refs is essential for building flexible, accessible component libraries. You have now completed the Context and Refs module.
